content.comment_body: Hello [product_name] community, thank you for your interest in [product_name] [version_no] with cloud integration. We've seen repeated inquiries about transferring [product_name] projects to AWS. The video demonstrates a workaround to help upload your project to AWS if the standard process doesn't work. I welcome feedback on the video. Best regards, [user_name]

Hi [user_name], I followed your video instructions and was able to upload the [product_name] program to AWS. Shortly after, I received an AWS email, similar to what another user described, confirming service activation. The program uploads fine in a different environment, but when controlling outputs via the web, the output doesn't respond, whereas it works correctly when loading it from the micro SD card of the [product_name] module. Thanks for your assistance.

Hello, There are several factors that might affect operation here: 1) Is the [product_name] correctly registered as a device? 2) Have you selected the correct AWS region? 3) Is the time configured properly on the [product_name]? 4) Are the correct values selected in your [product_name] table? Also, check under AWS IoT Core (shadow section) to confirm your [product_name] is sending data. Feel free to open a service request for individual support. Best regards
Hi [user_name], It turns out I forgot to mark the push buttons as writable. Thanks again for your help.

Hello everyone! I'm trying to upload a project to AWS. Steps taken: 1) Created an Amazon account; 2) Set up necessary policies (thanks to [user_name] for the guide); 3) Set up the XYZ app and environment; 4) Entered required info in [product_name]; 5) Checked signal flow in IoT, all signals pass; 6) Download starts and completes with no errors and a link is generated; 7) Clicking the link displays the site I created, but changes in data are not reflected; 8) In Elastic Beanstalk, there's no new application as expected. Questions: 1) What's causing this? Where is the downloaded site stored, and how do I link it to the environment? 2) Can an app and environment be created in the console and linked afterwards? How would this work?

Hi [user_name], 1.1 The download is located in Elastic Beanstalk -> Environments, where your created environments appear with their URLs. This is your access link. 1.2 Ensure your [product_name] is running. 1.3 Confirm the selected region is correct everywhere. 1.4 Make sure variables in [product_name] are connected to the correct device name. 2. I'm not sure I fully understood your question. To access the site, just save the link as a browser favorite or shortcut on your mobile device. If you encounter issues, consider opening a service request. Best regards, [product_name] Support
Will this setup only work with pushbuttons, or do switchbuttons function with AWS as well?

Hi [user_name], Both pushbuttons and switchbuttons work with AWS. However, using click mode may result in short pulses because the performance between [product_name], AWS, and the hardware isn't optimal. Your experience may also depend on which AWS IoT Core variation you use. Best regards, Tech Support
Good afternoon, where can I find the video in Spanish? Thank you.

Hi [user_name], Please try to post your question in English, as this is an international forum and responses are more likely in English. Here is the translation of your question. Regards, [user_name] Moderator
Hi, The workaround appears to function, but I'm seeing a deprecated platform status (see attachment). Is this normal?
If I follow the same process, I also see a 'Deprecated' message. However, the application runs as expected. As long as it works, you can disregard the warning. I consider this a workaround.

Hi [user_name], My setup was reliable for a year, but recently I encountered the same 'deprecated' issue and the system stopped working, prompting me to run the control from the microSD card instead. Today, I set up a new AWS environment with updated software, and while the deprecated warning is gone, deploying from [product_name] still doesn't restore proper functionality. The site and control interface load as expected, but no data is transmitted between the web portal and the hardware. This used to work fine before running into this warning, even though nothing in the program or setup changed. Any suggestions? Thank you.

Dear [user_name], Apologies for the delayed reply. Unfortunately, I can't diagnose this behavior precisely. If possible, please submit a service request for more targeted investigation. Service Request Greetings, [product_name] Support

Hello, Thanks for sharing. Following your workaround video, I built a sample program, and it worked. However, the link doesn't function properly on mobile devices. I also need to export the data log as an Excel file from the classic shadow for analysis. Could you advise how to achieve this?

analysis.insight_summary: Users are working to deploy cloud-connected [product_name] projects to AWS for remote monitoring and control. Many are experiencing issues where the AWS-hosted web interface does not properly control the device outputs, particularly when using push or switch buttons. Identified root causes include configuration mistakes in [product_name], such as not marking variables as writable, connectivity or region mismatches between [product_name] and AWS, and performance limitations impacting real-time control. Reliable integration remains a challenge, and troubleshooting efforts often involve reviewing device registration, regions, variable setup, and AWS IoT data flow.
analysis.user_expectations: Users seek straightforward integration for deploying [product_name] projects to AWS, enabling real-time hardware control and monitoring via the cloud interface. They expect clear guidance, dependable connectivity, smooth operation, and immediate device response from remote web controls.
